raised.claim: The authoritative scope can still be hijacked by a model-authored fenced block in `issue.body`, because that prose precedes the generated block and the parser takes the first block.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model includes ```triage-scope followed by valid scope JSON in its new-issue body, `parseScopeBlock` on the next run returns that model-authored scope instead of the validated scope appended by the job, allowing arbitrary attachments or making the issue unscoped.

raised.claim: Rows attached to proposed new issues are never checked against the proposed issue's scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal scoped to `candidates_count > 0`, or to `beer_ids: [1]`, can be referenced by a verdict for a zero-candidate row or beer 2; the issue is created and that contradicting row is reviewed against it, while the same attachment to an existing issue would be rejected.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not account for other verdicts accepted for the same issue earlier in the current plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: With `postCreationRows` equal to 11 and ten verdicts targeting that issue in one batch, every verdict observes 11 and passes, after which all ten rows are written and the issue reaches 21 post-creation rows despite `MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE = 12`.

raised.claim: Guard-hit counts are not logged when the model supplies a verdict for every row, even if the guards reject all of those verdicts.
raised.why_it_breaks: A single-row batch whose only verdict violates the issue scope has `covered === orphans.length`, so the warning is omitted although `plan.skipped` and `scope_violation` are both 1; the same rejection can recur daily without the promised one-line visibility.

raised.claim: A single empty probe is treated as proof of absence even when the other probe returned the beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the brewery probe returns empty but the name probe returns an exact matching beer, `proved` is true and a terminal `not_on_untappd` verdict survives despite direct search evidence that the beer exists.

raised.claim: Absence verdicts degraded by the new class gate are reported as `wontfix` in the outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: The gate pushes a quiet verdict with `review_class: 'matcher_bug'`; this loop's `else` then increments `wontfix`, so a run that merely lacked absence evidence publishes a digest claiming beers were deliberately classified wontfix.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END
raised.claim: Re-opening a failure on the candidates-count boundary clears its review fields but leaves the new `issue_number` link stale.
raised.why_it_breaks: A row reviewed against #347 and later re-failed across the 0↔>0 boundary gets NULL class, note, and review timestamp but retains `issue_number = 347`, so the column described as the authoritative row→issue link asserts an attachment for an untriaged row and corrupts subsequent issue audits.

raised.claim: The backfill always uses the first arrow/number anywhere in free-text notes rather than the trailing issue reference.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a legacy note such as `considered → #123, settled alias gap → #347`, the migration permanently assigns issue 123 although the actual attachment suffix names #347; model-authored notes were not constrained to contain only one arrow.

raised.claim: Appending the scope block to the end of issue bodies means it is omitted from the model prompt whenever the body exceeds 2000 characters.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a newly created issue with a long model-authored body, the next run parses and enforces the trailing scope but shows the model only the first 2000 characters; the model cannot see the attachment constraints and can repeatedly propose rows that the deterministic guard then skips.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: Lexicographically comparing timestamps with different valid ISO fractional-second formats can exclude a post-creation attachment.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub returns creation times such as `2026-08-14T06:00:00Z`, while reviews use `2026-08-14T06:00:00.000Z`; for an attachment in that same second after creation, the review string sorts before the creation string, so `reviewed_at > createdAt` is false and the row is omitted from saturation accounting.
